source.text: Ὅταν οὖν ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Δανιὴλ τοῦ προφήτου ἑστὸς ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω, τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη, ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι τὰ ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore you see the abomination of the desolation, the spoken through Daniel the prophet, standing in place holy (the reading let him understand), \v 16 then those in the Judea let them flee to the mountains, \v 17 the on the housetop not let him come down to take the things out of the house of him, \v 18 and the in the field not let him turn back behind to take the cloak of him.

en.L: So when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in [the] holy place (let the one reading understand), \v 16 then let those in Judea flee to the mountains; \v 17 let the one on the housetop not come down to take the things out of {{gender:their|his}} house, \v 18 and let the one in the field not turn back to take {{gender:their|his}} cloak.
en.B: So when you see the abomination that brings ruin, of which the prophet Daniel spoke, standing in the holy place (let the reader take note), \v 16 then those in Judea must escape to the hills. \v 17 Anyone on the roof must not go down to fetch things from the house, \v 18 and anyone in the field must not turn back for a cloak.
en.R: The prophet Daniel spoke about 'the horrible thing that brings ruin.' One day you will see it standing in the holy place. (Reader, think carefully about what this means.) \v 16 When that happens, people in Judea must run away to the hills. \v 17 If someone is up on the roof of a house, they must not go down to get anything from inside. \v 18 If someone is working in the field, they must not go back to get their coat.

decisions.choice: the abomination of desolation: the phrase from Daniel 9:27, 11:31 and 12:11
decisions.reason: In Daniel it is a detestable thing set up in God's sanctuary that leaves it desolate. In 167 BC the Syrian king Antiochus IV set up a pagan altar on the temple altar, and 1 Maccabees 1:54 uses the same phrase for it. Jesus says something like it will happen again.

decisions.choice: standing in the holy place: in the temple
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of the sanctuary, and the holy place most naturally means the temple. Here, unlike Mark 13:14, the word "standing" agrees with the thing, not with a person.

decisions.choice: let the one reading understand: an aside to the reader of the Gospel
alternatives: Jesus urging his hearers to understand Daniel when they read it
decisions.reason: The words speak of reading, not hearing, so they are most likely the Gospel writer's aside, as in Mark 13:14. They may instead be Jesus's call to understand what Daniel wrote, since Daniel too is told to understand (Daniel 9:23, 25).

decisions.choice: the housetop, the cloak: flat roofs reached by an outside stair, and the outer garment laid aside for work
decisions.reason: One could leave a flat roof by the outside stair without going indoors. A worker in the field laid the cloak aside. The danger will be so sudden that there is no time even for these.

decisions.choice: their or his (L); anyone ... a cloak (B); someone ... they (R)
decisions.reason: The commands apply to anyone. Literal offers "their" or "his" through the gender setting; Balanced and Readable use "anyone" and "they".

decisions.choice: the abomination that brings ruin (B); the horrible thing that brings ruin (R); let the reader take note (B); Reader, think carefully about what this means (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Daniel's phrase as it is. Balanced and Readable say what it means. Every level keeps the aside in parentheses.

source.text: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

records.literal_gloss: Woe but to those in womb having and to those nursing in those the days.

en.L: And woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
en.B: Woe to women who are pregnant and to those nursing babies in those days!
en.R: Those days will be very hard for women who are pregnant, and for mothers who are nursing babies.

decisions.choice: having in the womb: pregnant
decisions.reason: "To have in the womb" is the ordinary Greek way of saying a woman is pregnant.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and pity
decisions.reason: Here "woe" is not a curse on these women. It grieves for them, because they will find it hardest to flee.

decisions.choice: woe (L, B); will be very hard (R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Matthew, Literal and Balanced keep "woe". Readable says what the cry means.

source.text: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται ἡ φυγὴ ὑμῶν χειμῶνος μηδὲ σαββάτῳ·

records.literal_gloss: Pray but that not may happen the flight of you in winter nor on Sabbath;

en.L: And pray that your flight may not happen in winter, nor on a Sabbath.
en.B: Pray that you will not have to escape in winter, or on a Sabbath day.
en.R: Pray that you will not have to run away in the winter or on the Sabbath, the day of rest.

decisions.choice: winter: the cold, rainy season
decisions.reason: In Judea winter is the rainy season. Streams run high and roads turn to mud, so flight on foot would be hard.

decisions.choice: on a Sabbath: when travel was limited and help hard to find
alternatives: a rule that disciples must not flee on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Jewish custom limited how far one walked on the Sabbath (compare Exodus 16:29; Acts 1:12), and town gates and shops would be shut. Only Matthew mentions the Sabbath here, which may show that his first readers kept it.

decisions.choice: the day of rest
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Sabbath is, as in 12:1.

source.text: ἔσται γὰρ τότε θλῖψις μεγάλη οἵα οὐ γέγονεν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς κόσμου ἕως τοῦ νῦν οὐδ’ οὐ μὴ γένηται.

records.literal_gloss: Will be for then affliction great such as not has happened from beginning of world until the now nor not not may happen.

en.L: For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not happened from [the] beginning of [the] world until now, nor ever will.
en.B: For that will be a time of great distress, worse than anything that has happened since the world began, and nothing like it will ever happen again.
en.R: It will be a time of terrible trouble. Nothing like it has happened since the world began, and nothing like it will ever happen again.

decisions.choice: great tribulation such as has not happened: in the words of Daniel 12:1
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:1 speaks of a time of distress such as has never been since there was a nation. Jesus widens it to the whole history of the world.

decisions.choice: nor ever will: a double negative
decisions.reason: The strongest form of denial: there will never be another time like it.

decisions.choice: tribulation (L); distress (B); terrible trouble (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the long-used word, as in 24:9. Balanced and Readable use everyday words for great suffering.

source.text: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολοβώθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ· διὰ δὲ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς κολοβωθήσονται αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι.

records.literal_gloss: And if not were shortened the days those, not would be saved all flesh; because of but the elect will be shortened the days those.

en.L: And if those days had not been cut short, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be cut short.
en.B: Had those days not been cut short, not one person would come through alive. But for the sake of the chosen they will be cut short.
en.R: If God did not make that time shorter, no one would live through it. But God will make it shorter for the sake of the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen.

decisions.choice: cut short: a passive, God is the one who shortens the days
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. Mark 13:20 names him: the Lord shortened the days.

decisions.choice: any flesh: any human being
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for living people. "No flesh" means no one.

decisions.choice: be saved: survive, come through alive
decisions.reason: Here the word speaks of living through the distress, not of salvation at the end as in 24:13.

decisions.choice: the elect: the people God has chosen
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures the chosen are God's people. In this speech they are those who belong to God through Jesus (24:24, 31; compare 22:14).

decisions.choice: come through alive (B); live through it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that survival is meant, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: God did not make that time shorter; the people he has chosen
alternatives: those days had not been cut short; the elect
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who shortens the days and says what "the elect" means.

source.text: τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ὁ χριστός, ἤ· Ὧδε, μὴ πιστεύσητε·

records.literal_gloss: Then if anyone to you says, Look here the Christ, or Here, not believe;

en.L: Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here [is] the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}!' or 'Here!' do not believe [it].
en.B: If anyone says to you then, 'Look, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is here!' or 'He is here!' refuse to believe it.
en.R: At that time someone may tell you, 'Look, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is here!' or 'He is over here!' Do not believe them.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the promised king, said to have appeared in some place
decisions.reason: People will claim that the Messiah has come and can be found here or there. Jesus says his coming will not be like that (24:27).

decisions.choice: here, or here: two claims about different places
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats "here". Each speaker points to a different place.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: In speech the word points to something said to be in front of them, so it is kept at every level, as in 12:2.

decisions.choice: He is here (B); He is over here (R)
decisions.reason: The second claim is a single word in the Greek. Balanced and Readable make it a full saying. "He" is the claimed Messiah, not Jesus, so it takes no deity_pronoun span.

source.text: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται, καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα μεγάλα καὶ τέρατα ὥστε πλανῆσαι εἰ δυνατὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·

records.literal_gloss: Will arise for false christs and false prophets and they will give signs great and wonders so as to mislead, if possible, even the elect;

en.L: For false {{christos:christs|messiahs}} and false prophets will arise, and they will give great signs and wonders, so as to mislead, if possible, even the elect.
en.B: People falsely claiming to be the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} will rise up, and false prophets with them. They will work great signs and wonders, enough to lead astray even the chosen ones, if such a thing could be done.
en.R: People will come who falsely say they are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}. Others will falsely claim to be prophets. They will do great signs and amazing things. They will try to fool even God's chosen people, if they can.

decisions.choice: false christs: people who falsely claim to be the Messiah
decisions.reason: The word joins "false" and "Christ". It means pretenders to the title, as in 24:5.

decisions.choice: false prophets with signs and wonders: as in Deuteronomy 13:1-3
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 13:1-3 warns that a prophet may give a sign or wonder that comes true and still lead people astray. Signs alone do not prove a messenger is from God.

decisions.choice: if possible: they will try, but it may not be possible
decisions.reason: The phrase shows how strong the deception will be. It also suggests that God will keep his chosen ones from being led away (24:22).

decisions.choice: people falsely claiming to be the Messiah (B, R); the chosen ones (B); God's chosen people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the compound word means. Readable also says whose chosen people they are.

records.literal_gloss: Look, I have told beforehand you.

en.L: Look, I have told you beforehand.
en.B: Mark this: I have warned you in advance.
en.R: I am warning you now, before it happens.

decisions.choice: I have told you beforehand: the warning stands
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means the warning has been given and remains in force. When these things happen, the disciples will know they were told.

decisions.choice: look (L); Mark this (B); I am warning you now (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: ἐὰν οὖν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν· Ἰδοὺ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἐστίν, μὴ ἐξέλθητε· Ἰδοὺ ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις, μὴ πιστεύσητε·

records.literal_gloss: If therefore they say to you, Look in the wilderness he is, not go out; Look in the inner rooms, not believe;

en.L: So if they say to you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness,' do not go out; 'Look, in the inner rooms,' do not believe [it].
en.B: So if they tell you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness,' stay where you are. If they say, 'Look, he is hidden indoors,' do not believe it.
en.R: So if people tell you, 'Look, he is out in the desert,' do not go there. If they say, 'Look, he is hiding in a back room,' do not believe it.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: where would-be deliverers gathered their followers
decisions.reason: Leaders claiming to bring God's rescue led crowds out into the wilderness (compare Acts 21:38). Israel looked for a new deliverance like the exodus.

decisions.choice: the inner rooms: hidden rooms inside a house, a secret place
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 6:6 for the inner room where one prays. Some will say the Messiah is hidden away, known only to a few.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: As in 24:23, the word is part of what people say, so it is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: he, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: "He" is the one people claim is the Messiah, so the pronoun takes no span.

decisions.choice: stay where you are (B); he is hidden indoors (B); he is hiding in a back room (R)
alternatives: do not go out; in the inner rooms
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the second claim a full saying and say plainly what not going out means.

source.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἐξέρχεται ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ φαίνεται ἕως δυσμῶν, οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·

records.literal_gloss: Just as for the lightning goes out from east and shines as far as west, so will be the coming of the Son of the Man;

en.L: For just as the lightning comes out from [the] east and shines as far as [the] west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
en.B: The coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning that flashes in the east and lights up the sky all the way to the west.
en.R: When the Son of Man comes, everyone will see it. It will be like lightning that flashes across the whole sky from east to west.

decisions.choice: like lightning: sudden and seen by everyone
decisions.reason: Lightning cannot be hidden in a room or a desert. The coming of the Son of Man will not need anyone to point it out (24:23-26).

decisions.choice: coming: the arrival of the Son of Man in glory, as in 24:3
decisions.reason: The same word as in the disciples' question.

decisions.choice: the coming of the Son of Man first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the subject first so the comparison is clear.

decisions.choice: everyone will see it
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the comparison, following the meaning decision.

source.text: ὅπου ἐὰν ᾖ τὸ πτῶμα, ἐκεῖ συναχθήσονται οἱ ἀετοί.

records.literal_gloss: Wherever if may be the corpse, there will be gathered the eagles.

en.L: Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.
en.B: Where there is a dead body, that is where vultures flock.
en.R: Wherever there is a dead body, vultures will gather there.

decisions.choice: vultures: birds that gather at a dead body
decisions.reason: The word usually means eagle, and the eagle was the standard of the Roman legions, so some see a picture of Roman armies here. But the birds gather at a corpse, which is what vultures do, and the word was used of them too (compare Job 39:27-30).

decisions.choice: a proverb: the coming will be as plain as circling birds that show where a body lies
alternatives: judgment will fall wherever it is deserved
decisions.reason: The saying follows the picture of lightning (24:27), so it most likely means the coming cannot be missed. Luke 17:37 gives it in answer to the question "where?". Some read it of judgment falling on what is dead.

source.text: Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς, καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες πεσοῦνται ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: Immediately but after the affliction of the days those the sun will be darkened, and the moon not will give the light of it, and the stars will fall from the heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

en.L: And immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
en.B: Right after the distress of those days the sun will turn dark and the moon will stop giving its light. Stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
en.R: As soon as that time of terrible trouble is over, the sun will become dark. The moon will not shine. Stars will fall from the sky. The powers in the heavens will be shaken.

decisions.choice: sun, moon and stars: in the words of Isaiah 13:10 and 34:4
alternatives: a new prophecy with no source
decisions.reason: Isaiah 13:10 says the sun will be dark and the moon will not give its light; Isaiah 34:4 says the host of heaven will fall. Joel 2:10 speaks the same way.

decisions.choice: darkened sun and falling stars: the prophets' language for God acting in judgment
alternatives: only a description of the physical sky
decisions.reason: Isaiah used these words of the fall of Babylon (Isaiah 13). Such language marks a great act of God that shakes the world. How literally it is meant here is not certain.

decisions.choice: the powers of the heavens: the heavenly bodies, or spiritual powers ruling there
decisions.reason: "Powers" can mean the sun, moon and stars as the host of heaven, or spiritual beings. Both were thought of together.

decisions.choice: sky
decisions.reason: The same Greek word means both sky and heaven. Where stars fall, Balanced and Readable say sky.

source.text: καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὸ σημεῖον τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ τότε κόψονται πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς·

records.literal_gloss: And then will appear the sign of the Son of the Man in heaven, and then will mourn all the tribes of the earth and they will see the Son of the Man coming on the clouds of the heaven with power and glory great;

en.L: And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
en.B: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Every tribe on earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on heaven's clouds, with power and great glory.
en.R: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. All the peoples of the earth will cry out in sorrow. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds in the sky with power and great glory.

decisions.choice: the sign of the Son of Man: the sign the disciples asked for (24:3), perhaps the Son of Man himself appearing
alternatives: a separate sign in the sky, such as a banner or a cross
decisions.reason: The disciples asked for the sign of his coming. The verse does not say what it is. It may be the Son of Man himself, seen in heaven, or a signal that goes before him (compare the banner of Isaiah 11:12).

decisions.choice: all the tribes will mourn: in the words of Zechariah 12:10-14
decisions.reason: Zechariah says the people will look on the one they pierced and mourn, tribe by tribe. Here the mourning spreads to all the tribes of the earth.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven: Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: In Daniel one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven and is given authority, glory and an everlasting kingdom. Jesus will say the same before the high priest (26:64).

decisions.choice: the tribes of the earth: the peoples of the whole earth
alternatives: the tribes of the land of Israel
decisions.reason: The same words can mean "the tribes of the land", as in Zechariah. Beside the coming seen by all (24:27), they most likely mean all peoples.

decisions.choice: the sky (B, R); heaven's clouds (B); the clouds in the sky (R)
alternatives: in heaven; the clouds of heaven
decisions.reason: The same Greek word means sky and heaven. Balanced keeps Daniel's "clouds of heaven"; Readable says sky throughout.

decisions.choice: peoples; cry out in sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable uses common words, following the meaning decision on "tribes".

source.text: καὶ ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ μετὰ σάλπιγγος μεγάλης, καὶ ἐπισυνάξουσιν τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπ’ ἄκρων οὐρανῶν ἕως τῶν ἄκρων αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And he will send the angels of him with trumpet great, and they will gather together the elect of him from the four winds from ends of heavens to the ends of them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather together {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} elect from the four winds, from [one] end of [the] heavens to [the other] end of them.
en.B: As a great trumpet sounds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels. They will gather {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen ones from the four winds, from the farthest edges of the heavens on every side.
en.R: A loud trumpet will sound, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels. They will gather the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen from every direction, from one end of the sky to the other.

decisions.choice: the trumpet and the gathering: God's promise to gather his scattered people
decisions.reason: Isaiah 27:13 speaks of a great trumpet that calls the scattered home. Deuteronomy 30:4 promises to gather Israel even from the end of the heavens, and Zechariah 2:6 speaks of the four winds. Now the Son of Man gathers the chosen.

decisions.choice: the four winds, from end to end of the heavens: from every direction, everywhere
decisions.reason: The four winds are north, south, east and west. The ends of the heavens are where the sky seems to meet the earth on every side.

decisions.choice: his angels, his elect: the Son of Man has the angels and the chosen people as his own
alternatives: the angels and elect of God only
decisions.reason: What the Scriptures say belongs to God is here said to belong to the Son of Man, as in 13:41.

decisions.choice: with a great trumpet, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: with a trumpet and a great sound
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add a word for "sound" or "call". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the people he has chosen
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the elect" means, as in 24:22.
